def: properly, something received, i.e. (mentally) instruction (whether on the part of the teacher or hearer); also (in an active and sinister sense) inveiglement

occurrences.text: My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass:
For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.
A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:
For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.
With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him.
The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
